intent: Specify the baseline (table-driven, no SIMD) checksum update functions of `crc32fast::baseline`: `update_slow(prev: u32, buf: &[u8]) -> u32` and `update_fast_16(prev: u32, buf: &[u8]) -> u32` (Lean: `baseline.update_slow`, `baseline.update_fast_16`).

manual_mutants.note: fold_16 decodes the first word big-endian (only inputs of at least 16 bytes are affected)
manual_mutants.before: let i4 ← core.num.U32.from_le_bytes (Array.make 4#usize [ i, i1, i2, i3 ])
manual_mutants.after: let i4 ← core.num.U32.from_be_bytes (Array.make 4#usize [ i, i1, i2, i3 ])

manual_mutants.note: fold_16 forgets to xor the running crc into the first word (a fresh hash of 16 zero-prefixed bytes may still look plausible)
fold_16 looks up byte 10 in the table for byte 9's slot
corrupted entry 255 of slice-by-16 table 6 (reached only through fold_16 with byte 0xFF at offset 9 of a block)
corrupted entry 255 of the byte table (wrong only when (crc as u8) ^ byte == 0xFF)
fast path hands the folded state to update_slow without re-inverting it
the 16-byte tail loop skips 16 bytes without folding them
update_slow does not invert the incoming state: correct for prev = 0xFFFFFFFF only... (and wrong continuation)

bug_variants.source: https://github.com/srijs/rust-crc32fast/commit/210ad2198b3dfd804fc3ef5f25bc6d8a0fe1a13c (fix endianness bug in fast baseline impl)
bug_variants.note: pre-fix update_fast_16 xors the running crc into the first four bytes through `u32::from_le(crc)`, which byte-swaps the state on big-endian targets (rendered here as the big-endian behaviour: crc byte-swapped before the xor). Blocks of >= 16 bytes then get a wrong checksum unless the state is a byte palindrome; breaks fast == slow, CRC-32 test vectors and the incremental law

edits.after: let w0 ← (do let cb ← core.num.U32.to_le_bytes crc; let c ← core.num.U32.from_be_bytes cb; ok (i4 ^^^ c))
